pages.title: Export and sharing
pages.description: Export a Beam composition to MP4 or WebM with the right resolution and quality preset.
pages.lead: Export renders the current composition directly to a local file using the settings supported by the machine.

sections.title: Choose a format
bullets: WebM uses the WebM container with an encoder available on the current machine.
MP4 uses the MP4 container when Beam finds a compatible hardware or software encoder.

notice.title: Encoder availability
notice.text: A format can be unavailable when the machine does not provide a compatible encoder. Beam reports this before or during export.

sections.title: Choose a resolution
bullets: 720p scales down to an HD output when the native canvas is large enough.
1080p scales down to Full HD when the native canvas is large enough.
Max keeps the native output canvas dimensions.

sections.title: Choose quality and bitrate
paragraphs: Low, medium, and high presets calculate a bitrate from the output dimensions and frame rate. Medium balances clarity and file size, while high prioritizes visual fidelity.

screenshot.alt: Beam export settings for format, resolution, and quality
screenshot.caption: Select format, resolution, and quality before choosing the destination file.

sections.title: Monitor the export
paragraphs: Beam displays frame progress while rendering. You can cancel an active export or copy its diagnostic report. Live editor changes do not modify a file that is already rendering.

sections.title: Open the result
paragraphs: After a successful export, Beam reports the saved filename and provides an action to open the file. If export fails, copy the technical report before asking for help on [Discord](https://discord.gg/6Q6v2xUCB) or [GitHub](https://github.com/BeamRecorder/Beam/issues).

pages.title: Platform support
pages.description: Review Beam support and operating-system-specific behavior on Windows, macOS, and Linux.
pages.lead: Beam is available on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Native permissions and window-system capabilities create some differences between platforms.

sections.title: Windows
bullets: Beam is distributed as a native Windows installer.
Screen, window, region, camera, microphone, and system-audio recording are supported.
Overlay positions and sizes can be saved and restored.

sections.title: macOS
bullets: Beam is distributed as a DMG for Apple Silicon Macs running macOS 13 or newer.
Screen Recording, Microphone, and Camera permissions are requested when those sources are used.
Overlay positions and sizes can be saved and restored.

notice.title: Beam is damaged and cannot be opened
notice.text: After moving Beam to `/Applications`, run `xattr -cr /Applications/Beam.app`, or choose Open Anyway in System Settings > Privacy & Security.

subsections.title: Allow screen and system audio recording
paragraphs: Open Apple menu > System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen & System Audio Recording, then enable Beam. If Beam is not listed, use the add button and select `/Applications/Beam.app`. Quit and reopen Beam after changing this permission.

screenshot.alt: macOS Screen and System Audio Recording privacy settings with Beam enabled
screenshot.caption: Enable Beam under Screen & System Audio Recording.

subsections.title: Allow microphone and camera access
paragraphs: In System Settings > Privacy & Security, open Microphone and enable Beam when recording voice. Open Camera and enable Beam when using the camera overlay.

screenshot.alt: macOS Microphone and Camera privacy settings for Beam
screenshot.caption: Beam must be enabled in the privacy list for each source you want to capture.

sections.title: Linux
bullets: Beam is distributed as AppImage, DEB, and RPM packages.
Screen and window capture uses XDG Desktop Portal, PipeWire, and FFmpeg.
The system picker requests permission when a capture begins.
Keyboard shortcut and mouse click metadata requires explicit Polkit consent.
X11 can restore overlay positions and sizes.
Native Wayland can restore overlay sizes but not global positions.

notice.title: Wayland positioning
notice.text: Wayland does not expose global window coordinates. Beam does not force XWayland because that workaround can be incompatible with some GPU and X11 configurations.
